headline: High: TREK’s collaborative, browser/MCP-enabled defaults can amplify prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when paired with the unverified system_prompts_leaks source.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a is a source-available prompt-leak repository with no isolation or runtime controls shown, while agent_b is a real-time collaborative planner that uses browsers and MCP. That creates a plausible bridge where content from A can be ingested by B as instructions, especially through shared files or copied prompts. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b via MCP, browser, or shared files, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF agent_b treats imported text as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled prompts can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of external text into agent_b prompts.
Require provenance labels for any content imported from agent_a.
Review and strip instruction-like text before passing artifacts between agents.
Use a manual copy-paste step with human confirmation for any cross-agent transfer.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or prompt-firewalling between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b explicitly handles sensitive classes including API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and email addresses, and writes to local files plus logs. agent_a has no network egress and no data classes listed, but its prompt-leak focus makes it a plausible sink for sensitive material if paired in the same workflow. Because the pairwise data path is not directly evidenced, this is high rather than critical.
conditions: IF agent_b exports logs, uploads, or workspace files into agent_a-facing prompts, sensitive data can leak.
IF agent_a is used to inspect or summarize agent_b artifacts, secrets in those artifacts may be exposed.
mitigations: Exclude secrets and MFA material from any shared artifacts.
Rotate or redact API keys before cross-agent review.
Keep agent_b logs and uploads in a separate directory from any agent_a inputs.
Audit one sample transfer for accidental inclusion of confirmation numbers or credentials.
requires-engineering: enforce secret-scanning on all inter-agent handoffs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b supports multiple real-time collaborative instances and writes to files, while agent_a has no documented write surface or concurrency model. A direct write-write conflict is not proven, but agent_b’s shared mutable state plus the absence of any locking evidence means overlapping edits are plausible if A is used as a companion workflow. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF agent_a is used to generate or edit artifacts that agent_b also writes, concurrent modification conflicts can occur.
IF agent_b instances operate on the same travel.db or uploads path without locks, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working copies per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files.
Check file timestamps before saving merged outputs.
Limit agent_b to one active writer per workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking around travel.db and uploads.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it may operationalize outputs from agent_a if those outputs are presented as facts or prompts. agent_a’s prompt-leak orientation increases the chance that its text is treated as authoritative content rather than verified data. The pathway exists in default collaborative workflows, but no direct action-taking chain is documented.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without verification, errors can cascade into travel plans or reservations.
IF agent_a emits malformed or misleading instructions, agent_b may propagate them into downstream actions.
mitigations: Require a verification step before agent_b acts on agent_a output.
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted in the UI or prompt template.
Use a checklist for any reservation or itinerary changes derived from A.
Compare critical facts against a second source before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware gating for downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b touches country visit history, reservations, email addresses, and secrets, and its docs show self-hosted operation with file/log surfaces. agent_a is a source-available repository with no data residency controls described. The pair can therefore create retention and residency mismatch risks if agent_b data is copied into agent_a workflows, but the evidence is indirect and not specific to a regulated dataset.
conditions: IF EU personal travel data is exported from agent_b into agent_a-hosted tooling, residency and retention obligations may diverge.
IF agent_b logs or uploads are retained longer than intended, subject-rights handling can fail.
mitigations: Avoid moving personal travel records into agent_a artifacts.
Set a short retention window for agent_b logs and uploads.
Document where travel history and reservations are stored.
Redact email addresses before any cross-agent sharing.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
